title: VPC Onboarding — Cutover Tactical Cheatsheet (draft)
content:
Purpose and audience:
This document is a tactical, checklist-first cheatsheet to support customer VPC cutovers for Private Deployments (VPC / on-prem). Intended audience: Solutions engineers, SREs, customer network leads, and the onboarding PM. It complements the higher level onboarding playbook — think step-by-step actions, fast diagnostic commands, key Terraform knobs, and safe rollback hooks.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to private deployments that use: dedicated VPC peering / TGW, VPN or Direct Connect (or equivalent), and the Redwood edge service deployed in the tenant network.
- Assumes Terraform modules from infra/terraform-modules v2.3.x are in use; note module names used below.
- Not a security design doc. Follow customer compliance requirements for KMS/HSM, secrets, and audit configurations.

Pre-cutover quick health checks (run remotely before ticket start):
1) Verify baseline connectivity
   - ping from operator bastion to customer jump host: ping -c 3 <customer-jump-ip>
   - traceroute to control plane endpoint and model endpoints to validate expected path (note MTU / fragmentation).
2) Validate Terraform drift
   - git checkout onboarding-<tenant>; terraform init && terraform plan -var-file=tenant.tfvars -out=plan.out
   - If plan shows unexpected deletions, stop and escalate.
3) Confirm routing and BGP state (if applicable)
   - For BGP-connected DC: show ip bgp summary | grep <peer-asn>  (ensure Established)
   - Check prefix acceptance and MED/communities that might affect path.
4) TLS and KMS sanity
   - curl --resolve <control-host>:443:<ip> https://<control-host>/health -I
   - Confirm KMS key policies: aws kms get-key-rotation-status --key-id <key>

Cutover timeline (recommended windows and owners):
- T-72h: Run a dry run in staging with exact tenant.tfvars and module versions. Owner: SE.
- T-24h: Freeze config change window for customer infra. Owner: Customer network lead.
- T-2h: Final pre-cutover drift check and create rollback branches. Owner: SRE.
- T+0 to T+30m: Canary traffic and monitoring. Owner: SRE/SE.
- T+30m to T+3h: Ramp to 25/50/100% as acceptance criteria pass. Owner: SE/PM.

Minimal cutover checklist (execution order):
- [ ] Create a cutover channel and a dedicated incident bridge link. Post the runbook with step numbers.
- [ ] Tag the Terraform commit: git tag onboarding/<tenant>/cutover/<date> and push.
- [ ] Run terraform apply with auto-approve on a maintenance worker, capture stdout to artifact store. Command: terraform apply -var-file=tenant.tfvars plan.out | tee /tmp/tf-apply-<tenant>.log
- [ ] Validate security groups / firewall rules created match allowlist (do not open 0.0.0.0/0).
- [ ] Apply IP allowlist to customer fw and to Redwood control-plane ACLs simultaneously.
- [ ] If using TGW: attach route table and verify propagation. aws ec2 describe-transit-gateway-route-tables --filters ...
- [ ] Start canary: route 1–2% of requests to tenant endpoints via routing policy. Check request latency, token cost, and 5xx rates.
- [ ] Monitor logs for structured errors (parse for API error codes and rate-limit responses).
- [ ] Post-cutover: run acceptance suite (see "Acceptance tests" section).

Acceptance tests (automated where possible):
- Auth: token minting, renewal, and revocation flows succeed.
- End-to-end inference: small prompt execution within 300ms median for small models; larger model median within SLA agreed.
- KV cache warming: warm paths for common prefixes within first 50 requests.
- Telemetry: traces include tenant id, route id, model id. No sampling drop.

Rollback criteria and fast rollback steps (if any of these triggered):
- Criteria: sustained 5xx > 1% for 10m, latency SLA breach > 2x for 10m, or customer-network-reported packet loss > 5%
- Fast rollback: revert network-level routing (preferred) then revert terraform (if necessary). Commands:
   - Revert routing: update TGW/Route Table to previous attachment (document route table id in pre-cutover notes).
   - Terraform rollback: git checkout <pre-cutover-tag> && terraform apply -var-file=tenant.tfvars -auto-approve
- Post-rollback: run limited postmortem and a reduced-scope retest in staging before trying again.

Terraform-specific notes and common gotchas:
- Module pinning: always reference module source with version tag in root module: source = "git::https://git.company.com/infra/terraform-modules//vpc?ref=v2.3.1"
- State locking: ensure S3/remote backend and DynamoDB lock table are healthy. Command: aws dynamodb describe-table --table-name tf-state-locks
- Sensitive outputs: do not output secrets; use data sources for KMS keys and reference by ARN.
- Provider versions: pin aws/gcp providers in root to avoid drift: required_providers { aws = "~> 5.0" }
- Provider aliasing: tenant cross-account assume-role must be tested; sample snippet below.

Example provider snippet (annotated):
```
provider "aws" {
  region = var.region
}
provider "aws" {
  alias = "tenant"
  assume_role {
    role_arn = var.tenant_role_arn
  }
}
module "tenant_vpc" {
  source = "git::https://git.company.com/infra/terraform-modules//vpc?ref=v2.3.1"
  providers = { aws = aws.tenant }
  cidr_block = var.tenant_cidr
  enable_tgw = var.enable_tgw
}
```

Network-level hardening checklist (customer + Redwood):
- NTP: ensure NTP servers are reachable, prefer customer internal NTP; verify offsets < 100ms.
- MTU: ensure consistent MTU across cross-connects (9001 jumbo when available).
- Egress policies: deny all by default and explicitly allow control-plane endpoints + update servers.
- DNAT/SNAT: if customer uses SNAT, ensure return path to Redwood control hosts is allowed.
- Flow logs: enable VPC flow logs and route to short retention S3 bucket for 7–30 days; include sample retention policy in onboarding package.

Observability & SLO checks to have live during cutover:
- Latency (p50/p95/p99) per model endpoint and per route
- Error rate (4xx/5xx) with alert thresholds preconfigured for canary policy
- Token cost per request for high-volume routes
- Batching stats: average batch size, queue wait time, and timeouts

Customer handoff checklist (what we must confirm with customer before closing the onboarding ticket):
- [ ] DNS delegation and hostname certs issued + validated
- [ ] Firewall rules recorded and stored in the tenant onboarding doc
- [ ] Runbook shared with on-call rotation and escalation contacts
- [ ] KMS/HSM key material confirmed with rotation policy and backup plan
- [ ] Acceptance tests passed and artifacts attached to ticket

Post-upgrade follow-ups and small-batch optimization items (to be scheduled in 72 hours):
- Review token costs and suggest batching/quantization adjustments in Optimize recommendations
- Check cache hit ratios and tune prefix cache sizes for the tenant workload
- Validate autoscaling ramp thresholds are not oscillating; consider smoothing windows or scale-down cool-downs

Risk matrix (short):
- High: BGP misconfiguration, default route leaks, TLS cert mismatch
- Medium: TF state drift mid-apply, NAT gateway saturation, incorrect security-group ranges
- Low: metrics sampling misconfiguration, minor latency increase during cold starts

Field notes (lessons learned from prior cutovers):
- Run terraform apply in a CI runner with attached role rather than a laptop — reduces accidental local credential leaks.
- Always capture a full tgz of /var/log/redwood-agent on the tenant entry node for first 2 hours post-cutover.
- For customers with strict egress, prepare a pre-approved STUN/turn and external healthcheck list to avoid blocked probes.

Postmortem template (minimal):
- Incident summary (1–2 lines)
- Timeline with Timestamps (UTC)
- Triggering change (Terraform commit / routing edit / certificate rotation)
- Root cause and remediation
- Follow-up actions with owner and due date

Appendix: quick commands
- terraform fmt -check
- terraform init -upgrade
- terraform plan -var-file=tenant.tfvars -out=plan.out
- terraform apply -auto-approve plan.out | tee tf-apply.log
- aws logs tail /aws/route53/health --follow --start-time 2h
- curl -v --resolve <control-host>:443:<ip> https://<control-host>/livez

Notes and open questions:
- Decide if we should standardize on a single canary traffic controller (feature-flag-based) versus temporary route table adjustments per tenant. SE preference varies per customer risk profile.
- Need a small internal library of terraform helper scripts to extract pre-cutover route table snapshots and automatically restore them.

Owner notes: keep this cheatsheet lean and action-first. Move longer design explanations and compliance checklists into the onboarding-patterns handbook and link from here.

End of document.
